chunks: Three [narrators] - Abu Kurayb and Abu Sa'id said: Abu Usama narrated to us, he said: Al-Ash'ath narrated from Aamir, from his uncle, from Masrooq, who said:

We were sitting with Abdullah ibn Mas'ood, and he was reciting the Quran to us. A man asked him: 'O Abu Abdurrahman, did you ask the Messenger of Allah how many caliphs will rule this Ummah after him?' He said: 'No one has asked me about this since I arrived in Iraq! Yes, we asked the Messenger of Allah, and he said: Twelve, the number of the chieftains of the Children of Israel.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of caliphs after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Abdullah ibn Mas'ood, establishes the number of twelve successors as a prophetic decree, explicitly linking them to the twelve chieftains (anbiya' or quwwam) of the Children of Israel) mentioned in the Torah. In Shia scholarship, this narration is pivotal as it provides the Sunni-accepted basis for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing their divine appointment and continuity of leadership. The comparison to the Children of Israel underscores the structural and spiritual parallel between the earlier prophetic communities and the Islamic Ummah.
